**Finding: Compliant** (AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer)

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection or verification right running against Clear Capital. Key checks:

- **No audit clause exists.** Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verif", "books" returned nothing; "records" hits relate only to IP ownership (§4(b)) and the definition of Confidential Information (§7).
- **§3 Compensation is one-directional.** Contractor bills us with supporting detail (dates, hours, rates, receipts); there is no usage-reporting, self-declaration or true-up mechanic that a vendor audit right would attach to. Engagement is time-and-materials, so no under-licensing exposure.
- **The only access provision favours us.** §1 (p0007) requires *Contractor* to comply with Company's policies on access to and security of Company computer systems — the opposite of the walk-away concern about remote access to Customer systems.

Because no audit obligation is imposed on us, there is nothing to constrain on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access. This sits better than the playbook's preferred position, so no redline was proposed — inserting audit machinery would only manufacture a right the Contractor does not presently hold. Worth monitoring only if a future SOW introduces subscription, seat-based or usage-metered pricing, at which point audit limits should be negotiated at that time.
